subject: Linear combination of rw1 and SPDE model components at each observation time

messages.author: ef8463d2fe864477
messages.subject: Linear combination of rw1 and SPDE model components at each observation time
parts:
For the model
y = e^eta + eps_O
eta = 0 + mu + b + eps_L

I want to get the expected value and standard deviation of the mu + b (exluding eps_L) for each observation.
Mu is rw1 random effects model for about 1000 observation times (in the toy case below, the real world example has more)
b is an 8-group  random effect slowly varying in time, modeled as SPDE Gaussian process
eps_L is iid process variation at log scale - an identity random effect

I manged to create the set of linear predictors of the mu, but I do not know how to access the SPDE predictions at the projected times in the linear effect.
The following post describes uses the overall predictions, but in my case I only want some components of the linear predictor.
- https://groups.google.com/forum/embed/?parenturl=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.r-inla.org%2Fcomments-1&service=jotspot&ul=1&theme=default&place=forum%2Fr-inla-discussion-group&showpopout=true&showsearch=true#!searchin/r-inla-discussion-group/linear$20combination$20SPDE/r-inla-discussion-group/idPN7KXO8p0/VlcPIeMD-SQJ

I guess that they should be available by Predictor=i, for some indices, i.
There is a post describing the indices in r$summary.linear.predictor but I cannot transfer it to my case.
- https://groups.google.com/forum/embed/?parenturl=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.r-inla.org%2Fcomments-1&service=jotspot&ul=1&theme=default&place=forum%2Fr-inla-discussion-group&showpopout=true&showsearch=true#!searchin/r-inla-discussion-group/linear$20combination$20SPDE/r-inla-discussion-group/LRP5bTRHsUw/Py0htm-6AwAJ

The indices for the example below I get are
sapply(inla.stack.index(stack_est, "est"), length)
  data effects 
   8000   16048
 
So what is the index j in
lc1 <- inla.make.lincomb(Predictor=j)
to obtain the SPDE projection for time t and group i?
For the example below?

If I now this index, I can create the linear combinations for each observation.

Best regards
Thomas


mu0 = 1
sigma_b = 0.2
sigma_o = 0.1
sigma_pr = 0.05
n_gr = 8
n_obs = 1000
n = n_gr * n_obs
rho_b = 1000
times = seq_len(n_obs) - 1

# generate GP random effects
set.seed(0815)
cMatern <- function(h, range, nu = 1, kappa = sqrt(8*nu)/range) {
  ifelse(h > 0, besselK(h * kappa, nu) * (h * kappa)^nu /
    (gamma(nu) * 2^(nu - 1)), 1)
}
rmvnorm0 <- function(n, cov, R = chol(cov)) {
  crossprod(R, matrix(rnorm(n * ncol(R)), ncol(R)))
}
bCorr <- cMatern(as.matrix(dist(times)), rho_b, nu = 2)
b <- rmvnorm0(n_gr, sigma_b^2*bCorr)
b = b - mean(b)

# generate the synthetic data

epsl <- rnorm(n, sd = sigma_pr); epsl <- epsl - mean(epsl)
sigma_prs <- sd(epsl)
eps <- rnorm(n, sd = sigma_o); eps <- eps - mean(eps)
sigma_epss <- sd(eps)
df_exp <- tibble::tibble(
  gr = factor(rep(seq_len(n_gr), each = n_obs)),
  time = rep(times, n_gr),
  mu = mu0 + 0.15*sin(time/(2*pi*diff(range(times))/500)),
  #mu = mu0,
  b = as.vector(b),
  etab = .data$mu + .data$b,
  epsl = epsl,
  eta = etab + epsl,
  ytrue = exp(.data$etab + sigma_prs^2/2),
  eps = eps,
  y = exp(.data$eta) + eps,
  logy = log(.data$y),
  ytrue_plot = exp(mu + sigma_bs^2/2 + sigma_prs^2/2)
)

# Fit INLA model
  pr <- list(
    range_est_low = 400,
    prior_range = c(400, 0.01),
    prior_sigma_gr = c(0.2,0.8),
    prior_sigma_obs = c(0.2,0.8),
    prior_sigma = c(0.05,0.5)
    )
  ds_fit <- df_exp
  groups <- sort(unique(ds_fit$gr))
  n_gr <- length(groups)
  ds_fit$gr_int <- as.integer(factor(ds_fit$gr, labels = 1:n_gr))
  nbasis <- max(3,ceiling(diff(range(ds_fit$time)) / pr$range_est_low * 2.5))
  mesh <- inla.mesh.1d(
    seq(min(ds_fit$time), max(ds_fit$time), length.out = nbasis),
    degree = 2
  )
  spde_gr <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
    mesh = mesh,
    prior.range = pr$prior_range # for P(range <  x days) = 0.01
    , prior.sigma = pr$prior_sigma_gr # for P(sigma > x) = 0.01
  )
  iset <- inla.spde.make.index(
    "i",
    n.spde = spde_gr$n.spde, n.group = n_gr
  )
  amat <- inla.spde.make.A(
    mesh = mesh,
    loc = ds_fit$time, group = ds_fit$gr_int
  )
  prior_orig_prec <- list(prior = "pc.prec", param = pr$prior_sigma_obs)
  prior_log_prec <- list(prior = "pc.prec", param = pr$prior_sigma)
  group_effects <- data.frame(gr = ds_fit$gr_int, idx = seq_len(nrow(ds_fit)))
    stack_est <- inla.stack(
      data = list(y = ds_fit$y),
      A = list(amat, 1, 1),
      effects = list(iset, group_effects, data.frame(mu = ds_fit$time)),
      tag = "est"
    )
    sd_mu = 0.1
    log_tau_mu <- -2 * log(sd_mu) # short for log(1/sd_mu^2)
    formula <- y ~ 0 +
      f(mu, model = 'rw1', constr = FALSE, hyper = list(prec = list(
        fixed = TRUE, initial =log_tau_mu))) +
      f(i, model = spde_gr, group = i.group, control.group = list(model = 'iid')) +
      f(idx, hyper = list(prec = prior_log_prec))
    r <- inla(
      formula,
      data = inla.stack.data(stack_est),
      control.predictor = list(
        compute = TRUE,
        A = inla.stack.A(stack_est), link = 1
      )
      , control.family = list(
        control.link = list(model = "log"),
        hyper = list(prec = prior_orig_prec)
      )
      , control.compute = list(config = TRUE, dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
      control.inla = list(strategy = "adaptive",int.strategy = "eb"),
      control.results = list(return.marginals.predictor = FALSE,
                             return.marginals.random = FALSE)
    )

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Linear combination of rw1 and SPDE model components at each observation time
parts:
There are three ways to do this,

first is to use linear combinations, then if 'mu' have dimension m and
b have dimension k, the you need to define each one, like

lc1 = inla.make.lincomb(mu=1, b= 1)
names(lc1) = paste0("lc.1")

lc2 = inla.make.lincomb(mu=c(0,1), b= 1)
names(lc2) = paste0("lc.2")

etc,
where c(0,1), means 1*mu[2] ,and b=1, means 1*b[1]

and then join them together and add it to the call.

testit on a small example, before moving to the big one.


second, is to construct a fake linear predictor where you NA's out what
you do not need.

for this model
eta = 0 + mu + b + eps_L

you will have a data.frame with idx.mu, idx.b, and idx.epsL, say,

d = data.frame(y, idx.mu, idx.b, idx.epsL)

just make a new one where you pad with NA (note that the data is also
NA'ed in this part)

na = rep(NA, length(y))

d.new = data.frame(y=c(y,na), idx.y=rep(idx.y,2),
idx.b= rep(idx.b,2),
idx.epsL=c(idx.epsL, na))

in this way, the last half of the linear predictor, will contain the
linear combinations if mu+b

third, is to use inla.posterior.sample() and
inla.posterior.sample.eval()

r = inla(..., control.compute=list(config=TRUE))

xx = inla.posterior.sample(10000, r)

mu.b = inla.posterior.sample.eval(function() c(mu,b), xx)
## if these are the names... please fix

then each column will be a sample

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Linear combination of rw1 and SPDE model components at each observation time
parts:
Dear Håvard Rue,

thanks for describing the the tree ways to do this. I like option 2 and tried to implement it.
Setting idx.epsL= NA is way of omitting the error term in the predictions, that I would not have thought of.
For completeness, I provide the modified lines of the working example below.

Best regards
Thomas

amat <- inla.spde.make.A(
    mesh = mesh,
    loc = ds_fit$time, group = ds_fit$gr_int
 )

amat2 <- inla.spde.make.A(
    mesh = mesh,
    loc = rep(ds_fit$time,2), group = rep(ds_fit$gr_int,2)
  )
nas <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(ds_fit)
group_effects <- data.frame(gr = rep(ds_fit$gr_int,2L), idx = c(seq_len(nrow(ds_fit)), nas))
stack_est <- inla.stack(
      data = list(y = c(ds_fit$y, nas)),
      A = list(amat2, 1, 1),
      effects = list(iset, group_effects, data.frame(mu = rep(ds_fit$time,2L))),
      tag = "est"
)

n_obs <- nrow(df_fin)
  ind_obs <- inla.stack.index(res_fit$stack, "est")$data[seq_len(n_obs)]
  ind_mub <- inla.stack.index(res_fit$stack, "est")$data[n_obs + seq_len(n_obs)]
df_gr = data.frame(
      b = as.numeric(amat %*% r$summary.random$i$mode),
      etab = r$summary.linear.predictor$mode[ind_mub],
      y_pred = r$summary.fitted.values$mean[ind_mub]
)

On Thursday, June 18, 2020 at 8:22:52 PM UTC+2, Helpdesk wrote:
second, is to construct a fake linear predictor where you NA's out what
you do not need.

for this model

        eta = 0 + mu + b + eps_L

you will have a data.frame with idx.mu, idx.b, and idx.epsL, say,

d = data.frame(y, idx.mu, idx.b, idx.epsL)

just make a new one where you pad with NA (note that the data is also
NA'ed in this part)

na = rep(NA, length(y))

d.new = data.frame(y=c(y,na), idx.y=rep(idx.y,2),
                idx.b= rep(idx.b,2),
                idx.epsL=c(idx.epsL, na))

in this way, the last half of the linear predictor, will contain the
linear combinations if mu+b

Dear Håvard Rue and INLA users,

way 2 solved my specific problem but I do not yet fully understand how the linear combination approach (way 1) works.
I my understanding, specifying index into random effect b only provides me with the effects at mesh locations, but not the required random effects at the observation locations (In my example the location is time). I assumed to get the projections at observation locations I had to index into the prediction of effects. This idea seems to be not correct.

Could you, please, explain a bit more on how projections of SPDE components can be used in linear predictors?

Best regards
Thomas
On Thursday, June 18, 2020 at 8:22:52 PM UTC+2, Helpdesk wrote:

first is to use linear combinations, then if  'mu' have dimension m and
b have dimension k, the you need to define each one, like

lc1 = inla.make.lincomb(mu=1, b= 1)
names(lc1) = paste0("lc.1")
